answer: Admission auctions block fake identities by pricing scarce entry slots. Each epoch slots go to the highest escrowed bids. One genuine agent needs one slot, so its signal costs one bid, while a farmer must outbid rivals for every copy. At 40 units per slot, 1000 fakes cost 40000 units upfront. A caught fake forfeits its bid, a ripple that forces each seized slot to be rebought on the next voyage. An honest agent pays once for undiluted rewards.
